extracted.intended_audience: Fortune readers and general audience interested in tech, finance, and public policy (investors, business professionals, informed public)
extracted.subtask_short: reporting on billionaire tax and relocations
extracted.subtask_description: A business/news article describing wealthy individuals and entities moving assets or residences ahead of a proposed California wealth tax, including evidence, calculations, and perspectives. The piece situates the specific case (Larry Page) within broader context about tax policy and corporate/state relocation trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use primary documents/filings as evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: According to filings reviewed by Fortune, Page converted several entities out of California and incorporated them in Delaware on specific dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite state filings and corporate records (including dates and jurisdictions) to substantiate claims about incorporations, conversions, or corporate moves; present documentary evidence rather than relying solely on hearsay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek comment and disclose inability to reach subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Fortune could not reach Page for comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attempt to contact the people or organizations named in the story and explicitly report whether comment was obtained; disclose when a subject could not be reached to show due diligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and attribute anonymous sources and prior reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: An anonymous source told Business Insider that Page had left the state; Business Insider also first reported the conversions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relying on anonymous sources, identify the nature of the sourcing and attribute earlier or corroborating reporting from other outlets; be transparent about provenance and whether assertions are independently verified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detail policy mechanics and applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed tax calls for California residents with more than a $1 billion net worth to pay a one-time tax equivalent to 5% of their assets, payable over five years, with 90% allocated to health care, and retroactive to Jan. 1, 2026 if approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include precise details of the policy (thresholds, rates, payment terms, allocation of funds, effective/retroactive dates) so readers understand how the measure would operate and who it would affect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantify financial impact
rubrics_metrics.description: By that math, Page, worth about $270 billion according to the Bloomberg Billionaire Index, would owe the state roughly $13 billion if the proposal passed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use available net-worth estimates and straightforward calculations to translate policy proposals into concrete dollar impacts; show the assumptions and cite the valuation source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide historical and market context
rubrics_metrics.description: California's high levies and regulatory environment are often cited as reasons for businesses or wealthy individuals moving out; the article references Elon Musk's 2020 move to Texas and major companies that relocated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Situate the specific story in broader precedent and market trends (past relocations, tax differences across states, estimated tax savings) to explain potential consequences for innovation, capital, and state resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present multiple perspectives
rubrics_metrics.description: The piece contrasts those who are leaving California with figures who are unbothered by the proposal, such as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, and includes commentary from others like Garry Tan warning about capital flight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include viewpoints from different stakeholders—affected individuals, industry leaders, proponents and opponents of the policy—to provide a balanced narrative and surface competing interpretations of likely outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain legal and corporate-structural incentives for relocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Delaware, where Page incorporated several entities, does not require LLC owners to publicly disclose their names, which is one structural reason firms choose that jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe relevant legal, regulatory, or corporate-structural differences (privacy rules, disclosure requirements, tax regimes) that create incentives for incorporation or relocation decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribute and credit prior reporting and sources
rubrics_metrics.description: The article references and credits reporting by Business Insider and The New York Times and notes which outlet first reported particular elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When building on other media reports, credit those outlets and, where relevant, indicate novelty (which outlet first reported) and any corroboration undertaken by the current piece.
